details:
Currently, one of my avatars needs to have a looping ambient sound transition from 3D to 2D to help it sound better at close distance while not being intrusive at a larger distance.

Traditionally, in Unity, the audio curve for spatialization can be manipulated (see the green line in the first attachment) to achieve this goal. This curve makes it such that as distance approaches 0 meters, the audio transitions from a 3D source into a 2D source dynamically.

Audio sources that employ the use of of the spatialization curve will not function this way in VRChat. Instead, they will behave as if they are unambiguously 2D sources. This is somewhat misleading as it does work in the Unity editor as expected; it is only in-game that it fails.

The current workaround is to set the audio to completely 3D, then use the Spread (blue) curve to disperse the audio across the stereo channels of the listener as they approach. This works decently well but is not perfect as the effect changes depending on the orientation of the listener.
title: Audio spatialization curves do not work on avatars, always behave as 2D.
